fills.explanation: The captive light ascends over the earth and rises up before being revealed in the atmosphere between, paralleling the upward motion described in each cloud's ascent pattern throughout the chapter.

Direct parallel with ¶6 (water cloud) where the sign "shall come in the atmosphere in various forms and are heard" — fire corresponds to sight and water to hearing, so the fire cloud's flashes "are seen" just as the water cloud's booms "are heard."

The lives are "purified by her towards receiving the light" — in both Manichaean and Swedenborgian frameworks, purification is directed toward the capacity to receive divine light/wisdom; "receiving" is the fundamental purpose of the Virgin's purifying action upon the captive lives.
The Virgin reveals the light "to it" (the cloud), consistent with the parallel in ¶3 where she "shall display to it" — the cloud is the recipient of her displayed light.

Confirming the editor's choice: "these angels" designates the specific group of divine truth-agents assigned to seize the expelled rulers, consistent with Kephalaia usage for known celestial functionaries.
The angels come beside "them" (the rulers), causing the rulers to flee — the pronoun refers back to the rulers who are the object of the angels' pursuit throughout ¶4.

The rulers "assume whatever they meet upon and go into" things — mirroring the paired verbs in ¶4 where rulers "go into whatever they will meet upon and assume it," with the same two actions (assume/go into) in reversed order.

The rulers enter into things "that they did not seek" — they act chaotically and without purpose, seizing whatever they encounter indiscriminately, consistent with the Manichaean teaching on demonic chaos and ¶4's image of the robber fleeing without direction.
Confirming the editor's choice: "the children of fire" uses the definite article to identify the rulers as offspring of the fire element, a standard Kephalaia designation for this class of archons.
Confirming the editor's choice: "the cloud" takes the definite article as the specific cloud of water, paralleling "the cloud" in each of the five element sections.

fills.fill: The lives in it shall be purified
fills.explanation: Every cloud section includes a statement on the purification of the lives; parallel passages confirm this: ¶10 has "shall the lives be purified," ¶11 has "The lives in it shall be cleansed," and ¶12 has "the lives are purified in it."
Confirming the editor's choice: the rulers are constrained "in a" water cloud, using the indefinite article for a general cloud formation from which they flee.
Confirming the editor's choice: "they too are so" refers to the water rulers who fled, following the same destructive pattern as the fire rulers described in ¶5.
Confirming the editor's choice: "every place that they will reach" is the standard formulaic expression used throughout the chapter for the rulers' destructive contact with places (¶5, ¶7, ¶12).

The water rulers ruin seed-corn, fruits, and plants, and they "shall destroy" every place they reach — parallel to the fire rulers who "burn and destroy" in ¶5, expressing the universal devastation wrought by stripped rulers.
Confirming the editor's choice: "every place that they will reach" uses the relative pronoun "that," consistent with the identical construction repeated throughout the chapter.

The wind rulers make waves in the rivers and seas and "raise them up" — referring to the waters being lifted, a natural maritime image for the spiritual turbulence caused in flowing truths and gathered knowledge.
The wind rulers "overturn" the ships, corresponding spiritually to the overturning of doctrinal systems; overturning is the natural action of storm-winds upon vessels at sea.
The wind rulers "wreak destruction in them" — referring to the rivers and seas just mentioned, where the rulers cause waves, storms, and overturn ships.
The wind rulers "seize and bring them to the deep" — ships and their passengers dragged to the depths, corresponding to doctrinal truths being plunged into the deepest natural obscurity.

fills.fill: and it shall come above towards the likeness of
fills.explanation: All five cloud sections require the cloud to ascend toward the Virgin's likeness — ¶3, ¶6, ¶9, and ¶12 all use this formula; the five-fold structural pattern very strongly constrains this medium gap to contain the ascent toward the Virgin.
The Virgin "shall display its sign too to it" — she shows the sign to the cloud, matching the formulaic "display to it" used in ¶3 and ¶9 for the Virgin's presentation to each ascending cloud.

Direct parallel with ¶10 (wind cloud) where rulers "descend from it, safe in their image" — the phrase describes rulers retaining their own form after being stripped from their cloud, a consistent feature across the stripping descriptions.

The rulers "come forth from it" (from the light cloud), paralleling ¶10 where rulers "descend from it" and ¶12 where rulers "come from it" — the standard phrasing for rulers emerging from their stripped cloud.

The rulers cause destruction "there until the angels seize them" — a temporal limit on their destruction, consistent with the pattern in every section where angels are eventually dispatched to constrain the rulers.

Correcting the editor's "the image": all parallel cloud passages use "the likeness of the Virgin" (¶3: "towards the likeness of the Virgin of Light"; ¶9: "towards the likeness of the Virgin"), making "the likeness" the consistent formulaic term.

Every cloud section describes "the lives" being purified — ¶10: "shall the lives be purified," ¶11: "The lives in it shall be cleansed," confirming that "the lives" is the subject purified within each cloud.

The strong structural pattern across all five cloud sections shows purification "in stillness and rest/calm" followed by "Again, the rulers that will be stripped" — confirmed by ¶10 and ¶11 which use identical transitional formulas.
The compound "find and reach" parallels the formulaic "reach and arrive at" in ¶10, where paired verbs of contact describe the rulers' encounter with their targets throughout the chapter.

The air-cloud rulers "make it like one of" something — "like" is the natural comparative connector in the Kephalaia for describing how rulers transform what they possess into their own corrupt nature, paralleling ¶4's description of how rulers corrupt every place they touch.

The rulers make things "like one of the dead" — directly paralleling ¶4 where rulers "shall make dead and a loss" every place they touch; "the dead" is the standard Kephalaia category for what rulers reduce living things to.

The formulaic phrase "the hour when" appears in ¶16 of this same chapter ("until the hour when those rulers will be stripped"), establishing it as the text's own temporal formula for appointed moments of divine intervention.

Answering ¶14's question "to what place do those seven ditches go down?" — "paths" pairs with "ditches" as used later in the same chapter ("seven outer paths that are in the great sea"), and "go down" echoes the question's own verb.
The ditches descend through the earths below "to the" feet of the Porter — the preposition connects the spatial descent to its terminal point at the cosmic foundation-keeper.

The rulers assume "the tree and the flesh" — the paired terms for perception and corporeal will; confirmed by the next line which references "tree and that of flesh" as the two domains the rulers possess.

The angels "set a watch over them, that they might guard them" — a watch (surveillance post) is the natural-plane expression for divine truths establishing protective containment over imprisoned evil affections until the appointed hour of their stripping.
The rulers "shall be gathered together above" — the standard phrasing for collective assembly of stripped entities before their reformation and judgment, paralleling Manichaean gathering formulas.

The rulers "are poured out again in their first forms and images" — "again" marks the reconstitution back into their original states, consistent with the Kephalaia's pattern of rulers being reformed into their primordial shapes before final judgment and extraction of light.

Completing "for[ms and im]ages" — "forms and images" is a standard Kephalaia hendiadys pair for the original archetypal states of the rulers, into which they are reconstituted before their light is extracted and they are cast down.
